clue.text: Wager on group providing storage space?

parts.note: to back a horse is to bet on it
a pack is a group, as of wolves or cards

explanation.surface: A betting syndicate is somehow the source of extra room for keeping things.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack carried on the shoulders is portable room for stowing belongings.

clue.text: Game bishop on long mountain range

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a ridge is a long narrow stretch of high ground

explanation.surface: A cleric plays a match on a long chain of peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge is a card game for four players in pairs.

clue.text: This should help being poor form in bed

parts.note: a creature is a living being

indicators.note: in puts the reworked letters inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: poor form is bad shape, so the letters are mangled

explanation.surface: Someone poorly in bed needs a little luxury to feel better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' (as in poor form, bad shape) yields MFOR, put 'in' COT; the definition leans on the whole sickbed picture, so the clue is nearly all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: A small luxury such as warmth or good food is meant to ease and help one's wellbeing.

clue.text: Jab and run game

parts.note: to poke is to jab
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Prod someone and flee: a playground game.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker is a card game of betting and bluffing.

clue.text: Looking back this'll show the way forward

definitions.text: Looking back this'll show the way forward

parts.words: Looking back this'll show the way forward
parts.note: road studs reflect headlights straight back at the driver, marking the lane ahead at night

explanation.definitionFit: Reflective studs set in British roads, named after a cat's shining eyes, guide drivers in the dark.

clue.text: American energy drink exhausts

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: An American energy drink leaves you worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume something completely is to exhaust it, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: This finds its own goal alone

definitions.text: This finds its own goal alone

parts.words: This finds its own goal alone
parts.note: a guided weapon steers itself onto its target without help

explanation.definitionFit: A guided bomb uses lasers or GPS to steer unaided to its target.

clue.text: Check an exit with Isle of Man racing

indicators.note: the Isle of Man is famous for TT motorcycle racing, which here churns the letters

explanation.surface: Inspect an exit used in the Isle of Man TT races.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man TT is a famous motorcycle road race, which makes 'racing' look like scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-examination is a check of oneself, as for symptoms or one's conscience.

clue.text: The joke is he would become grounded perhaps?

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
he'd is the contraction of he would

explanation.surface: A bad joke would get him grounded.
explanation.walkthrough: HED is HE'D with the apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A grounded teenager is being punished, so grounding is one example of punishment.

clue.text: Runner cools little woman

parts.note: to ice something is to chill it
Kate is a pet form of the woman's name Katherine, so a 'little' version of it

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps a small woman chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: A skate's blade runs over the ice, so it can be called a runner, as a sledge's blade is.

clue.text: Slough holds everyone down!

indicators.note: holds says one piece grips the other within it

parts.note: a slough is a bog or marsh, as is a fen
all means every person

explanation.surface: Everybody in the Berkshire town of Slough is feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is also an English town, so the capital disguises the marsh sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has dropped to the ground is down, a simple synonym.

clue.text: Some relish a revealing game

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tasty sauce exposes some meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hares are hunted and eaten as game.

clue.text: Grand adult hill beast?

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A creature living on a big grown-up hill.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal shortening for an alligator, a reptile and so a beast by example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Precision engineering cases next

indicators.note: engineering means working or contriving the letters into a new form

explanation.surface: Accurate engineering of the casings comes next.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactness and precision are synonyms for being strictly accurate.

clue.text: Goalkeeper's beginning to stimulate game

indicators.note: beginning asks for the opening letter of the goalkeeper

parts.note: to rouse is to stir up or excite

explanation.surface: A keeper's first job is to fire up the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goalkeeper' and 'game' suggest football, but game here is wild birds shot for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The red grouse is a classic game bird shot in Britain.

clue.text: Dawn with pound wandering this way then that?

indicators.note: wandering means roaming about, so the letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: Walking about at dawn with a pound in your pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving up and down is going in one direction then the other.

clue.text: Call from the dead moggy in Bacchic cry

indicators.note: in says the cat goes inside the cry

parts.note: evoe is the exclamation of Bacchic revellers
moggy is British slang for a cat, often an ordinary one

explanation.surface: A cat in the middle of a drunken shout summons spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To evocate is to evoke or summon up, as a spirit raised by necromancy.

clue.text: Flogged unusually pure fat coating

indicators.note: a coating wraps around, so the fat surrounds the other letters

parts.note: lard is pig fat

indicators.note: unusually means in an odd way, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: Cooking talk: unusually pure fat coats something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges PURE to RUPE, coated by LARD.
explanation.definitionFit: To larrup is a dialect word for to thrash or beat.

clue.text: No longer used every day, broken chair blocks up a cupboard's front

indicators.note: something that blocks up a gap sits inside it, so the chair goes in between
front asks for the cupboard's first letter
a broken chair has its parts rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken chair is jammed against a cupboard's front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocks up' looks like a verb about obstruction; here the broken chair (RCHAI) fills the space between A and the C at the cupboard's front.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic words and things are antiquated, no longer in ordinary current use.

clue.text: Pirate game

definitions.meaning: to pirate is to copy unlawfully
short for cribbage, a card game

explanation.definitionFit: Cribbing is copying, and crib is also the card game cribbage.

clue.text: Game's poor performer

definitions.meaning: in British sport a ... is a weak player, as a tail-end batsman at cricket or a duffer at golf

explanation.definitionFit: Both a hunted animal and, in sporting slang, an unskilled player.

clue.text: Paper on bird's music

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
bird is British slang for a prison sentence, which is time served

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about a bird's song.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtime is a syncopated piano music style from the US.

clue.text: What this is again … a game

parts.note: this text is a crossword clue
do is short for ditto, meaning the same again

explanation.surface: A puzzle-solver's musing on what they are reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Cluedo is a British board game of murder detection.

clue.text: Right, I need gym somehow sorting out

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come together in some unstated arrangement

explanation.surface: Fixing things properly means I must get to the gym somehow.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedying a problem is putting it right, a synonym for sorting it out.

clue.text: Stole quiet tool

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
an awl is a pointed tool for piercing leather

explanation.surface: Someone stole a tool on the quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' reads as the past of steal; it is the noun, a scarf worn over the shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: A stole is a wrap worn over the shoulders, the same garment family as a shawl.

clue.text: Steal end of the game

parts.note: snip is slang for a steal or bargain

indicators.note: end of asks for the final letter of the word the

explanation.surface: Pinch the closing moments of the match.
explanation.definitionFit: The snipe is a wading bird shot as game.

clue.text: Enemy, we hear, turn over and son snaps

indicators.note: we hear says the word for the enemy is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a foe is an enemy
TO is the abbreviation for turn over, printed at the foot of a page
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: An enemy apparently turns over and his son takes pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Snaps are casual photographs, an informal synonym.

clue.text: After a fashion Clive is India's first to develop

indicators.note: after a fashion means in some rough way, so the letters are reshaped
first asks for the opening letter of India

explanation.surface: Clive is roughly the first to develop India, a colonial-history scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After a fashion' scrambles CLIVE IS with I, India's first letter; Clive of India was the British colonial general.
explanation.definitionFit: To civilise a society is to bring it to a more advanced, developed state.

clue.text: Taking out awkward Aussie involves dough

indicators.note: involves says one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: dag is Australian slang for an awkward or socially inept person
tin is old slang for money, as is dough

explanation.surface: Going out with a clumsy Australian who has money.
explanation.definitionFit: Dating someone is taking them out on romantic outings, an idiom.

clue.text: Either on mobile or into this thing

indicators.note: mobile means movable, so the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Get it on your mobile phone or put it into this gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning into this place or matter.
